newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Constantinescu sweeps to power in Romania.
newsitem.headline: Constantinescu sweeps to power in Romania.

text.p: Centrist reformer Emil Constantinescu defeated incumbent Ion Iliescu in Romania's presidential election on Sunday, ending a long period in power for ex-communists.

Television exit polls said Constantinescu won by around eight percent in Sunday's presidential run-off race, completing a historic rejection of leftist forces begun with a parliamentary victory for reformers two weeks ago.
Iliescu, a senior communist official under Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, immediately appeared at a news conference to concede defeat and congratulate his rival.

The victory ends the grip ex-communists have held on power in the Balkan country since the 1989 revolution which the opposition have always claimed was a popular revolt used by top Ceausescu functionaries to seize control.
Constantinescu quickly appeared on television to deliver a resounding victory speech.
"Romanians have decided without hesitation what there future will be this decade," he said. "We were voting at a crossroads in history for Romania's place in the world."
His speech drew rapturous applause from hundreds of supporters for whom the victory was the final chapter in the 1989 revolution they believed stolen for them.

When the result was announced thousands of students erupted in joy in the city's main University Square, site of bloody shootings during the 1989 revolt and miners riots that crushed opposition forces in 1990 and 1991.
Firecrackers exploded in the night sky and cars drove through the city streets with their horns blaring.
Constantinescu's triumph ends seven years of rule by ex-communists in the only Eastern European country not to have elected opposition forces in the modern era.
